title: Ad-hoc staffing + cost spark slate (May 2027)
body:
Purpose:
Small, fast-running ad-hoc sheet to estimate staff effort and incremental cost for a short surge/triage window (May 15–21, 2027). Use to make quick handoff decisions and call out blockers. Not a replacement for formal capacity planning; keep lightweight.

Quick summary: total estimated headcount-days: 18.5 -> est incremental cost (labor only): $14.2k for 1 week (assumptions below). Primary drivers: burst SRE coverage for new rollout, SE triage for 2 enterprise customers, patch QA.

---
Mini table (rows are short-hand; owners flagged for follow-up):

| Owner           | Role                | Est FTE days (15–21 May) | On-call? | Cost/day (USD) | Est cost (USD) | Notes / follow-up |
|-----------------|---------------------|--------------------------:|:--------:|---------------:|---------------:|-------------------|
| Marcus Chen     | SRE (runtime)       | 5.0                      | Yes      | 900            | 4,500         | Need to confirm swap with core oncall (Slack #sre-swap) |
| Priya Patel     | Solutions Eng (SE)  | 3.0                      | No       | 700            | 2,100         | Customer A hands-on triage; add runbook link |
| Evan Rodriguez  | QA (automation)     | 2.5                      | No       | 600            | 1,500         | Quick regressions + smoke for canary build |
| Aisha Martinez  | Product Ops         | 1.0                      | No       | 650            | 650           | Coordination, updates to rollout matrix |
| Lina Kovács     | Support (tier 2)    | 2.0                      | No       | 450            | 900           | Ticket overflow window (9–5 PT) |
| Tom Baker       | SEC/INFSEC review   | 0.5                      | No       | 1,100          | 550           | Quick config sign-off for dedicated clients |
| Floating pool   | Contingency (rotation) | 4.5                   | Variable | 700 avg        | 3,150         | Reserve pool for next-day spikes |

Subtotal headcount-days: 18.5
Subtotal labor cost (sum of est cost): $13,350
Buffer/overhead (7% ops overhead + incidental cloud tests): $930
Grand total (labor + buffer): $14,280

Assumptions used:
- "Cost/day" is loaded fully-burdened approximate cost (salary + benefits + bench) for quick internal decisioning; not an invoice.
- Contingency pool uses 700/day average to avoid undercounting mixed roles.
- We are not including additional cloud burst fees here — separate quick scan exists in linked artifact (confluence/ops/surge-coverage-2027).

Priority buckets (for deciding who to pull first):
1) Customer escalations (Priya) — must keep ≤4h MTTR baseline for customer A/B.
2) Runtime stability at canary (Marcus + Evan) — if error rate > 0.3% escalate to circle.
3) Security gating (Tom) — stop-gap if any reg fails.
4) Ticket backlog > 30 items — pull support pool.

Quick action checklist (today):
- [ ] Marcus: confirm SRE swap time with core oncall (deadline: 2027-05-12 EOD).
- [ ] Priya: share customer A debug logs link and primary contact. (done? check Jira JIRA-OPS-4521).
- [ ] Evan: smoke test script run and artifacts to /artifacts/canary/2027-05-15.
- [ ] Aisha: publish 1-paragraph update to #ops-brief and tag stakeholders (done by 09:30 PT 2027-05-15).
- [ ] Lina: set support overflow playbook (link) and quick KB for common asks.

Unresolved questions / risks: 
- Do we have capacity to cover night-zone (UTC 00:00–06:00) without additional hire? (Status: likely partial — see contingency pool).
- If canary rollback is needed, what is our 30-minute lane for automated re-routing? (Owner: eng-platform, ticket GH#1129).
- Will dedicated customers require extra legal sign-off for the temporary config change? (Owner: Tom — dependent on SEC review).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this sheet tight; move formal allocations into the monthly capacity sheet if surge exceeds 10 business days.
- If cost exceeds $20k, escalate to Director for approval per finance policy.

Communication template (for quick updates to stakeholders):
Subject: Short surge coverage plan (May 15–21) — quick headcount + cost
Body (1-liner): Triage window planned; est 18.5 headcount-days, ~$14.3k incremental labor (buffer incl). Focus: customer triage + canary stability. Will update on 5/17 with actual burn.

Postmortem triggers (if any apply next week):
- Overrun > 30% of estimated headcount-days
- Incident with Sev1 customer impact
- Any security gating failure that delayed rollout > 2 hours

Last quick calc log: 2027-05-11 14:22 PT — initial pass by A.M.; rates pulled from internal cost matrix v2027-03.

Slack references / quick links:
- Slack: #sre-escalation, #ops-brief, #se-triage
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-4521 (customer A triage), JIRA-ROLL-311 (canary rollout)
- Confluence: confluence/ops/surge-coverage-2027 (detailed cost scan)

If you are reading this and need a deeper breakdown by hour or by region, ping me and I can split the contingency pool into APAC/EU/NA buckets (5-minute job).

-- Aisha

(working draft — keep in shared_drives/company/misc for quick edits; will move to product-ops capacity binder if we repeat this pattern)
